title: STEM Application in Education: Implication of STEM Computational Paradigm on Employment Prospects
venue: Journal of Science, Management and Technology
extended_summary:
This paper discusses the role of STEM education and computational thinking in preparing learners for employment in an increasingly automated digital economy. It frames artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing, and related technologies as part of a broader STEM computational paradigm that is reshaping education, work, and sustainable development. Rather than evaluating a specific classroom intervention, the article surveys and synthesizes prior literature and workforce statistics to argue that STEM competencies are central to employability, innovation, and national development.

A substantial portion of the paper focuses on how ChatGPT and other generative AI tools can support teaching and learning. The authors describe ChatGPT as a writing coach, a tool for generating questions, supporting peer review, scaffolding communication, and helping teachers promote critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving in STEM instruction. The discussion is presented at a conceptual level, with examples of how educators might use generative AI to support lesson activities and student skill development.

The paper is not an empirical study of a defined sample of teachers or students; instead, it is a theoretical and exploratory review drawing on published sources from 2022–2024 and on labor-market data. The main conclusion is that technology, including generative AI, can strengthen STEM education and support sustainable development goals, but successful use requires improved teacher preparation, access to instructional resources, and attention to digital divide and ethical concerns. The article especially emphasizes the importance of preparing teachers to integrate computational thinking and AI-supported pedagogies across subjects.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative, exploratory review/opinion piece rather than a primary empirical study. It does not report a clear evaluation design, comparison group, or original outcome data for the AI intervention discussed.
impact_tier_rationale: No measurable intervention effect is reported, so there is no evidence of impact size on learning, teaching, or institutional outcomes. The paper is conceptual and theoretical, not an outcomes study.

interventions.use_case: Descriptive discussion of ChatGPT as a writing coach and classroom support tool for teachers and students, including generating questions, outlines, feedback on drafts, and support for critical thinking, peer review, and communication in STEM learning.
